predecessors.name: Maadi culture
predecessors.text: Lower Egypt and the Faiyum: Buto, Tell Ibrahim Awad, Tell el-Rub'a, Tell el-Farkha and Maadi, the Maadian sites "vacated" or conquered

successors.name: Early Dynastic Period of Egypt
successors.text: Egypt from the Delta to the First Cataract

ledger.x: 4000 BCE: the Naqada culture, Egypt's Predynastic, rises in Upper Egypt.
3650 BCE: Naqada II, the Gerzean, begins: "Naqada II (about 3650-3300 BC)", "represented throughout Egypt".
3300 BCE: Naqada III, the Protodynastic, begins: "Naqada III (about 3300-2900 BC)", "coterminous with the Protodynastic Period" ("Early Bronze Age c.
3200 BCE: Upper Egypt absorbs the Delta.
3000 BCE: the First Dynasty; Cliopatria's Early Dynastic Period of Egypt begins.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture confined to the Nile valley: the desert edge is sharp by nature, the southern limit toward Nubia and the northern limit against the Maadian are soft.
